run.researchNotes: Batch 1 of 4: sectors 01-12 of 41 (CONTINUE for 13-41). Returns: latest consistent close is 31-10-2026 (NSE month-end dashboard), not 20-11-2026; Nifty 50 rose ~10% in early November, so figures understate the November rally for all indices, benchmark included. Returns are total-return-index figures (NSE dashboards publish TRI), about 0.5-3% a year above price returns depending on dividend yield. m6 is chained from monthly/quarterly dashboard figures. Business growth is the simple average of MOFSL coverage YoY growth for Q3 FY26, Q4 FY26 and Q2 FY27, because the Q1 FY27 sector table could not be extracted. earningsGrowth3y is a 2-year CAGR (FY26-FY28) from MOFSL sector aggregates, because no 3-year sector forecasts were found. demandGrowth3y is mostly a 1-year FY27 forecast from rating agencies, with the span given in 'years'. P/E is the NSE-published trailing figure on 20-11-2026; no 5-year averages were found, so every sector lacks pe5yAvg. Bellwether symbols are given for the application's own price check. 'searchesRun' counts searches plus page fetches.

sectors.name: Banking

returns.source: NSE Indices Index Dashboards (niftyindices.com) for 31-May-2026, 30-Jun-2026, 30-Sep-2026 and 31-Oct-2026; m3 and y1 as printed on 31-Oct-2026; m6 chained as (1+May 1M)(1+Jun 1M)(1+Jul-Sep 3M)(1+Oct 1M)-1. Total-return index, not price return.

business.period: Q3 FY26, Q4 FY26 and Q2 FY27 (Q1 FY27 sector table not retrievable), each YoY; simple average of quarterly growth
business.basis: MOFSL coverage: Banks-Private (12) and Banks-PSU (6), equal-weighted average of the two segments; revenue = MOFSL 'sales' (NII-based)

tailwinds: Private banks posted 25% YoY PAT growth in Q2 FY27 (MOFSL), and MOFSL models ~21% EPS growth for them in both FY27E and FY28E.
System credit was growing 18-19% in late October 2026, with corporate, retail and MSME all contributing (ICRA).
risks: ICRA expects credit growth to slow to 15-16% for FY27 as higher policy rates weigh on loan demand in H2.
ICRA flags rising fresh slippages at both public and private banks; unsecured personal and MSME loans are ~17% of non-food credit.
outlook.source: MOFSL Aug-2026 valuation snapshot (EPS growth: private 21.0%/20.8%, PSU 9%/14% for FY27E/FY28E, averaged); ICRA banking outlook reported 28-10-2026 (credit growth 15-16% FY27)

valuation.source: NSE Indices published trailing P/E via marketcalls.in NSE index valuation dashboard (20-11-2026). Long-run median P/E 16.4 since 2003; 5-year average not published there.

sectors.why: Earnings are compounding in the high teens while the index trades at 14.3x trailing earnings against a long-run median of 16.4x.

sectors.name: Non-banking finance

returns.source: NSE Indices Index Dashboards (niftyindices.com) for 31-May-2026, 30-Jun-2026, 30-Sep-2026 and 31-Oct-2026; m3 and y1 as printed on 31-Oct-2026; m6 chained as (1+May 1M)(1+Jun 1M)(1+Jul-Sep 3M)(1+Oct 1M)-1. Total-return index, not price return.

business.period: Q3 FY26, Q4 FY26 and Q2 FY27, each YoY; simple average of quarterly growth

outlook.years: FY26 to FY28 (earnings, 2-year); FY26 to FY27 (AUM)
tailwinds: Crisil sees NBFC AUM growing 18-19% a year through FY27, crossing Rs 50 lakh crore by March 2027.
Gold-loan NBFC AUM is expected to grow ~40% annualised over FY26-FY27 with credit costs under 1% (Crisil).
risks: Unsecured MSME loans (~6% of NBFC AUM) show rising delinquencies; Crisil expects their growth to slow to 13-14% from 31%.
Funding: bank lending to NBFCs was only marginally above year-ago levels, so access to funds will drive divergence (Crisil).
outlook.source: MOFSL Aug-2026 valuation snapshot (NBFC EPS growth 22.8% FY27E, 18.3% FY28E); Crisil Ratings NBFC outlook (Nov-2025) and gold-loan report

valuation.source: NSE Indices published trailing P/E via marketcalls.in NSE index valuation dashboard (20-11-2026). Long-run median P/E 21.43 since 2022; 5-year average not published there.

sectors.why: Lending NBFCs are growing profits fastest in financials, but the Ex-Bank index has fallen 12.9% in three months, so price has not followed earnings yet.

sectors.name: Insurance

returns.source: NSE Indices Index Dashboards (niftyindices.com) for 31-May-2026, 30-Jun-2026, 30-Sep-2026 and 31-Oct-2026; m3 and y1 as printed on 31-Oct-2026; m6 chained as (1+May 1M)(1+Jun 1M)(1+Jul-Sep 3M)(1+Oct 1M)-1. Total-return index, not price return.

business.period: Q3 FY26, Q4 FY26 and Q2 FY27, each YoY; simple average of quarterly growth

tailwinds: Emkay expects life-insurance retail APE to grow 11-12% in FY27, with private insurers at 13-14%.
Retail health is the fastest-growing general-insurance line; the industry grew ~7% in gross direct premium in Q2 FY27 (Emkay).
risks: Pending commission regulations are pressuring life-insurance stocks (Emkay, Sep-2026).
Motor-insurance price competition keeps general-insurance growth modest in FY27 (Emkay, Oct-2026).
outlook.source: Emkay Research life insurance note (08-09-2026) and general insurance note (23-10-2026)

valuation.source: NSE Indices published trailing P/E via marketcalls.in NSE index valuation dashboard (20-11-2026). Long-run median P/E 25.83 since 2026; 5-year average not published there.

sectors.why: Premium growth is steady at about 11-12%, but the index is down 19.8% in a year on commission-rule worries, and the 5-year valuation history is short.

sectors.name: Capital markets

returns.source: NSE Indices Index Dashboards (niftyindices.com) for 31-May-2026, 30-Jun-2026, 30-Sep-2026 and 31-Oct-2026; m3 and y1 as printed on 31-Oct-2026; m6 chained as (1+May 1M)(1+Jun 1M)(1+Jul-Sep 3M)(1+Oct 1M)-1. Total-return index, not price return.

business.period: Q3 FY26, Q4 FY26 and Q2 FY27, each YoY; simple average of quarterly growth
business.basis: MOFSL coverage: NBFC-Non Lending (16-19) for Q3/Q4 FY26, Capital Markets (18) for Q2 FY27

outlook.years: FY26 to FY28 (earnings, 2-year); FY26 to FY30 (MF AUM)
tailwinds: Mutual-fund quarterly average AUM rose 14.1% YoY to Rs 89.51 lakh crore in Q2 FY27 (ICRA Analytics).
Retail MF AUM grew 14.2% in the six months to September 2026 as household savings shift to market products.
risks: The index runs 1.3x market beta, so revenue tracks market volumes and volatility.
At 45x trailing earnings the index is above its median, leaving little margin for a volume slowdown.
outlook.source: MOFSL Aug-2026 valuation snapshot (NBFC-Non Lending EPS growth 28.0% FY27E, 17.3% FY28E); Bajaj AMC MD via Business Today (03-09-2026): MF AUM to double by FY30; ICRA Analytics (28-10-2026)

valuation.source: NSE Indices published trailing P/E via marketcalls.in NSE index valuation dashboard (20-11-2026). Long-run median P/E 44.72 since 2024; 5-year average not published there.

sectors.why: It is the only financial index with a positive 1-year return (+14.1%) on 20%+ earnings growth, but it trades at a premium of 45x.

sectors.name: Fintech and payments

tailwinds: UPI handled 24,162 crore transactions worth Rs 314 lakh crore in FY26 (Grant Thornton).
Payment-services revenue is forecast to compound 22.1% a year to 2032 as take rates rise (Ken Research).
risks: Most UPI volume carries zero or very low merchant fees, so volume growth outpaces revenue.
UPI growth is moderating at scale (Grant Thornton India Payments Trends 2026).
outlook.source: Ken Research India Payment Services Market (Sep-2026); Grant Thornton India Payments Trends 2026

sectors.why: Digital-payment volumes keep compounding, but profit depends on monetising low-fee rails, which is unproven at sector scale.

sectors.name: Information technology

returns.source: NSE Indices Index Dashboards (niftyindices.com) for 31-May-2026, 30-Jun-2026, 30-Sep-2026 and 31-Oct-2026; m3 and y1 as printed on 31-Oct-2026; m6 chained as (1+May 1M)(1+Jun 1M)(1+Jul-Sep 3M)(1+Oct 1M)-1. Total-return index, not price return.

business.period: Q3 FY26, Q4 FY26 and Q2 FY27, each YoY; simple average of quarterly growth (INR terms)

tailwinds: Nifty IT rose 18.1% in October 2026, the best sector that month, from a low base.
Nasscom puts FY26 AI services revenue at $10-12 billion and expects it to rise significantly.
risks: ICRA projects only 3-5% USD revenue growth for FY27 because traditional services demand is weak.
GenAI productivity gains are compressing traditional run revenue per employee.
outlook.source: MOFSL Aug-2026 valuation snapshot (Technology EPS growth 10.0% FY27E, 6.8% FY28E); ICRA IT services half-yearly update (31-08-2026)

valuation.source: NSE Indices published trailing P/E via marketcalls.in NSE index valuation dashboard (20-11-2026). Long-run median P/E 24.1 since 1997; 5-year average not published there.

sectors.why: Price momentum has turned sharply up and valuation is near its 20th percentile, but forecast growth is the weakest of any large sector.

sectors.name: Pharmaceuticals

returns.source: NSE Indices Index Dashboards (niftyindices.com) for 31-May-2026, 30-Jun-2026, 30-Sep-2026 and 31-Oct-2026; m3 and y1 as printed on 31-Oct-2026; m6 chained as (1+May 1M)(1+Jun 1M)(1+Jul-Sep 3M)(1+Oct 1M)-1. Total-return index, not price return.

business.period: Q3 FY26, Q4 FY26 and Q2 FY27, each YoY; simple average of quarterly growth
business.basis: MOFSL coverage: Healthcare (28-31 companies, pharma plus hospitals)

tailwinds: ICRA estimates 13-15% domestic-market growth in FY27 for its sample set, helped by GLP-1 launches and price rises.
Crisil says export growth is broadening beyond the US, supporting 11-13% sector revenue growth in FY27.
risks: Crisil expects raw-material and freight inflation to trim margins by 150-200 bp in FY27.
US generics price erosion, including lower lenalidomide sales, is slowing US revenue.
outlook.source: MOFSL Aug-2026 valuation snapshot (Healthcare EPS growth 9.3% FY27E, 21.8% FY28E); Crisil Intelligence (28-09-2026); ICRA pharma update

valuation.source: NSE Indices published trailing P/E via marketcalls.in NSE index valuation dashboard (20-11-2026). Long-run median P/E 34.59 since 2005; 5-year average not published there.

sectors.why: It is the strongest index over 6 and 12 months (+17%, +23%), but it trades at 45.7x against a 34.6x median, its 83rd percentile.

sectors.name: Healthcare services

returns.source: NSE Indices Index Dashboards (niftyindices.com) for 31-May-2026, 30-Jun-2026, 30-Sep-2026 and 31-Oct-2026; m3 and y1 as printed on 31-Oct-2026; m6 chained as (1+May 1M)(1+Jun 1M)(1+Jul-Sep 3M)(1+Oct 1M)-1. Total-return index, not price return.

business.period: Q3 FY26, Q4 FY26 and Q2 FY27, each YoY; simple average of quarterly growth
business.basis: MOFSL coverage: Healthcare (28-31 companies; same aggregate as Pharmaceuticals because MOFSL does not split out hospitals)

outlook.years: FY26 to FY28 (earnings, 2-year, MOFSL Healthcare aggregate); FY27 to FY28 (hospital revenue)
tailwinds: ICRA expects hospital revenue to grow 13-15% in FY27 and 15-17% in FY28 as new beds ramp up, with ARPOB up 6-8%.
Occupancy was 63.5% in FY26 and ARPOB rose 9.2%, and ICRA keeps a Positive outlook.
risks: The Nifty Healthcare Index trades at 47.2x, its 100th percentile and +2.96 SD above median.
Heavy bed-addition capex dilutes margins until new hospitals ramp up.
outlook.source: ICRA Hospital quarterly update (30-07-2026); MOFSL Aug-2026 valuation snapshot

valuation.source: NSE Indices published trailing P/E via marketcalls.in NSE index valuation dashboard (20-11-2026). Long-run median P/E 37.58 since 2020; 5-year average not published there.

sectors.why: It has the clearest revenue visibility of any sector (13-17% a year), but valuation is at a record high.

sectors.name: Chemicals

returns.source: NSE Indices Index Dashboards (niftyindices.com) for 31-May-2026, 30-Jun-2026, 30-Sep-2026 and 31-Oct-2026; m3 and y1 as printed on 31-Oct-2026; m6 chained as (1+May 1M)(1+Jun 1M)(1+Jul-Sep 3M)(1+Oct 1M)-1. Total-return index, not price return.

business.period: Q3 FY26, Q4 FY26 and Q2 FY27, each YoY; simple average of quarterly growth

outlook.years: FY26 to FY28 (earnings, 2-year); FY27 (specialty chemicals revenue, 1-year)
tailwinds: Q2 FY27 sales rose 25% YoY for MOFSL's chemicals coverage, and Equirus finds median revenue up 22% across 72 listed chemical firms in Q1 FY27.
The agrochemical industry is expected to return to 8-10% growth in FY27 as exports recover (Crisil).
risks: Crisil sees specialty-chemical revenue growth slowing to ~6% in FY27 on weak exports and higher input costs.
Chinese overcapacity caps prices; returns on capital may take 2-3 years to recover (Equirus).
outlook.source: MOFSL Aug-2026 valuation snapshot (Chemicals EPS growth 28.3% FY27E, 13.6% FY28E); Crisil Ratings specialty chemicals (02-07-2026); Equirus (02-10-2026)

valuation.source: NSE Indices published trailing P/E via marketcalls.in NSE index valuation dashboard (20-11-2026). Long-run median P/E 43.87 since 2025; 5-year average not published there.

sectors.why: Revenue is recovering but profits are not yet, and the index is falling at 41x earnings.

sectors.name: Fertilisers

tailwinds: The government raised NBS subsidy rates for H2 FY27, roughly doubling nitrogen and tripling sulphur rates (ICRA).
Subsidy outgo is expected at about Rs 1.9 lakh crore in FY27, which supports availability (ICRA).
risks: ICRA's outlook is Negative: rupee depreciation and scarce sulphur and ammonia from the West Asia conflict squeeze margins.
Crisil warned domestic urea and complex output could fall 10-15% if LNG and ammonia disruptions persist.
outlook.source: ICRA fertiliser updates (Mar-2026, Sep/Oct-2026, report 7208 on H2 FY27 NBS rates); Crisil Ratings (Mar-2026)

sectors.why: Volume growth is only 1-3% and ICRA rates the outlook Negative, so near-term earnings depend on subsidy policy.

sectors.name: Automobiles

returns.source: NSE Indices Index Dashboards (niftyindices.com) for 31-May-2026, 30-Jun-2026, 30-Sep-2026 and 31-Oct-2026; m3 and y1 as printed on 31-Oct-2026; m6 chained as (1+May 1M)(1+Jun 1M)(1+Jul-Sep 3M)(1+Oct 1M)-1. Total-return index, not price return.

business.period: Q3 FY26, Q4 FY26 and Q2 FY27, each YoY; simple average of quarterly growth
business.basis: MOFSL coverage: Automobiles (26-31 companies, OEMs and ancillaries)

tailwinds: PV wholesale volumes grew 29% YoY in 5M FY27 (ICRA), and Maruti sold a record 2,76,120 vehicles in October 2026.
MOFSL's automobile coverage grew Q2 FY27 PAT 34% YoY on 30% sales growth.
risks: ICRA expects FY27 wholesale growth to slow to 3-6% on a high base after GST-led demand.
OEM price hikes and a weak monsoon could dampen rural demand in H2 FY27 (ICRA).
outlook.source: MOFSL Aug-2026 valuation snapshot (Automobiles EPS growth 16.8% FY27E, 26.9% FY28E); ICRA PV update (30-09-2026) and auto outlook (Feb/Mar-2026)

valuation.source: NSE Indices published trailing P/E via marketcalls.in NSE index valuation dashboard (20-11-2026). Long-run median P/E 30.48 since 2011; 5-year average not published there.

sectors.why: Earnings are accelerating (Q2 PAT +34%), but the index fell 11.4% in three months because the market doubts volumes after the GST boost.

sectors.name: Auto components

returns.basis: index (total return); Nifty Auto is OEM-heavy, so it is a proxy for components
returns.source: NSE Indices Index Dashboards (niftyindices.com) for 31-May-2026, 30-Jun-2026, 30-Sep-2026 and 31-Oct-2026; m3 and y1 as printed on 31-Oct-2026; m6 chained as (1+May 1M)(1+Jun 1M)(1+Jul-Sep 3M)(1+Oct 1M)-1. Total-return index, not price return.

business.period: Q3 FY26, Q4 FY26 and Q2 FY27, each YoY; simple average of quarterly growth
business.basis: MOFSL coverage: Automobiles aggregate (includes ancillaries; MOFSL does not split out components)

outlook.years: FY26 to FY28 (earnings, 2-year, MOFSL Automobiles aggregate); FY27 (component revenue, 1-year)
tailwinds: ICRA projects 7-9% component revenue growth in FY27 on replacement demand, premiumisation and an export recovery.
Margins held at 11.0-11.5% in FY27 through price pass-through and indexation (ICRA).
risks: US import tariffs have already hurt export earnings (ICRA).
Rare-earth magnet supply from China is a constraint, especially for EV parts.
outlook.source: ICRA auto outlook (27-03-2026) and auto component update (report 7123, 2026)

valuation.source: NSE Indices published trailing P/E via marketcalls.in NSE index valuation dashboard (20-11-2026). Long-run median P/E 30.48 since 2011; 5-year average not published there.

sectors.why: Replacement demand gives components steadier 7-9% growth than OEM volumes, but there is no separate index and figures borrow from autos.
